content_voiceover: This slide looks ahead at where higher risk M D S treatment is heading. Allogeneic transplant remains the dashed line backbone for anyone eligible. Everything else branches off next generation sequencing, which lets you match mutations to targeted drugs, F L T 3 inhibitors for F L T 3 mutations, enasidenib for I D H 2, ivosidenib for I D H 1, and eprenetapopt for T P 53, though that last one is marked with an X since it failed to show benefit. Other pathways like splicing factors, N or K RAS, and T E T 2 point toward investigational agents such as rigosertib or vitamin C. On the right, the H M A plus backbone is being explored with new biomarker guided combinations, but notice how many partners are crossed out, sabatolimab, venetoclax, magrolimab, and pevonidestat all failed to pan out in trials. What did succeed is oral cedazuridine slash decitabine, known as A S T X 7 2 7, giving an oral H M A option, and I R A K 4 inhibitors remain an open question mark.
keypoints: Allograft remains the definitive option for eligible patients
NGS-directed therapy: FLT3i, enasidenib for IDH2, ivosidenib for IDH1
Eprenetapopt, sabatolimab, venetoclax, magrolimab, pevonidestat all failed trials
Oral cedazuridine/decitabine (ASTX727) is an approved oral HMA
Open questions remain around checkpoint blockade and MRD markers
keypoint_voiceover: The exam relevant takeaway is knowing which HMA combination trials failed, venetoclax, magrolimab, sabatolimab, and pevonidestat all disappointed in higher risk M D S, while oral cedazuridine decitabine succeeded and is now a real option. Keep NGS driven, mutation targeted therapy in mind as the future direction.
